You need that to for him, but... Well...

segments.title: Hatchet, the Memphis pianist of the 1920s
segments.summary: Interviewer asks about a pianist called Hatchet who accompanied a singer in 1920s Memphis; Sunnyland Slim describes him as a tall piano player and talks about Memphis associates.

segments.title: Tommy and Tony Jackson, Little Brother Montgomery and Asa Slim
segments.summary: Talk of Tommy Jackson, Tony Jackson's sisters in Chicago, Little Brother Montgomery's drawing power and another pianist and his women.

segments.title: Tape chatter and a piano song demonstration
segments.summary: Room talk, a bawdy piano song and repeated chatter before the tape ends.

segments.title: Palmer interview: compositions, birth, teachers, piano greats, Margaret Johnson records
segments.summary: The second session starts inside one block: Palmer's tunes, birth in 1901 and Georgia upbringing, Fats Waller and James P. Johnson, Longshaw, Bessie Smith's husband, and the Margaret Johnson recordings.

segments.title: Floyd Jones's whereabouts
segments.summary: Brief talk about where Floyd Jones lives in Chicago and his love of fishing.

segments.title: Personnel of the Buddy Doyle recordings
segments.summary: Asked who played on the Buddy Doyle sessions, Slim says he was on them and names Jack Kelly and Fred McDowell, whom he later toured overseas with.

segments.title: Keg House and Big Boy Cruder: musicians known only by name
segments.summary: Slim says he knew of Keg House and had little dealing with Big Boy Cruder, whose brother was in Chicago.

segments.title: Steady Roll: multi-instrumentalist partner at Cairo
segments.summary: Slim recalls working with Steady Roll around Cairo and Missouri, the poisoned-alcohol quarrel, and learning chords from him.

segments.title: P. R. Gibson, the boss Memphis pianist
segments.summary: Slim corrects the name to P. R. Gibson and praises his schooling, style and playing for the Union.

segments.title: Playing blues and church songs with feeling; early pay at picture shows
segments.summary: Slim says blues must be played with feeling, credits Little Brother, and recalls his low early pay playing at silent picture shows.

segments.title: Singing and tuning chatter
segments.summary: Tape-recording remarks, a sung blues about the devil, and talk of keys.

segments.title: Memphis piano players: Florida Street Snooki and Big Maceo
segments.summary: Slim names Memphis pianists, describes Florida Street Snooki's playing and Big Maceo's left hand and stroke.

segments.title: Albino Red and Bob Koester
segments.summary: Slim remembers running with Albino Red in 1928-29 and the record man on Grand Avenue who owed him money from the 1964 overseas trip.

segments.title: Alan Shaw and Peetie Wheatstraw as one man
segments.summary: Interviewer and Slim discuss whether Alan Shaw and Peetie Wheatstraw were the same man and where he came from.

segments.title: Delta Joe, Roll and Tumble and meeting Little Brother
segments.summary: Slim says he recorded as Delta Joe, discusses Roll and Tumble versions, the Vicksburg blues and when he met Little Brother.

segments.title: Guitarists, bands and Willie Dixon's Big Three in Chicago
segments.summary: Slim names guitar players, describes his small bands and says blues drew the work when Dixon came in.

segments.title: Back to Hatchet and Sergeant Hatchet; Roosevelt Sykes in 1931
segments.summary: Slim identifies Hatchet, his nicknames, his limited style and his link to Roosevelt Sykes in 1931.

segments.title: Margaret Johnson recording group and its players
segments.summary: Palmer names the band behind Margaret Johnson, including McKeever, Nanton and Elmer Williams, used on recordings for OKeh.

segments.title: Identifying Margaret Johnson's titles and the 1926 session
segments.summary: Interviewer reads titles; Palmer recognises the Delaney songs and confirms he played on the 1926 Victor titles.

segments.title: Session personnel, June Clark and turning down Bessie Smith
segments.summary: Palmer lists the band, says he was with June Clark and led his own outfit, and reflects on Margaret Johnson versus Bessie.

segments.title: Joe Jordan's session, Wilberforce band and later compositions
segments.summary: Palmer recalls recording with Joe Jordan's group, his Wilberforce college band tour in the East, knowing Duke and Basie, illness and his unpublished songs.

segments.title: Jerome Carrington and the Mosley brothers in Chicago
segments.summary: Palmer recalls musicians he met on arriving in Chicago, Jerome Carrington and the Francois Mosley band at the Golden Lily.

segments.title: Albert Ammons and Indiana Avenue
segments.summary: Palmer talks about Albert Ammons, working alternate weeks at the Indiana Avenue theater and when they met.

segments.title: Clarence Jones, teaching and Little Brother Montgomery
segments.summary: Palmer talks about Clarence Jones, his health and teaching career, and when he first knew Little Brother.

segments.title: Interviewer's travel plans
segments.summary: Palmer asks about the interviewers' route and timing to Memphis, Mississippi, New Orleans and Europe.
